source_review.notes: Checked all ten final DoD, NASA, and NIST references on 2026-08-31; every final URL returned HTTP 200. Replaced an expired transient SD-22 PDF URL with the stable official ASSIST record for the active 2026-01-06 document. Reviewed SD-22, active NASA MSFC-STD-3620, NIST CSF 2.0 implementation examples and patch/configuration guidance, NASA CM/risk/data/operations guidance, and NPR 7123.1B. Hardware/DMSMS and institution-specific scopes are kept explicit.

evidence: Reviewed required service horizon, support horizon, resolution lead time, review time, and decision-slack notation with consistent units.
Reviewed obsolescence issue tuple for identity, usage, population, horizon evidence, consequence, uncertainty, alternatives, evidence, ownership, and triggers.
Reviewed lifetime-buy demand balance and its explicit planning-only assumptions.
Confirmed end-of-sale, last order, last shipment, maintenance/security support, suitability, availability, and practical interpretability are not overloaded.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation supports horizon and option-loss reasoning without presenting uncertain estimates as universal formulas.

evidence: Executed obsolescence-horizon-fixture under python3 with exact output in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-086/report.json.
Confirmed six declared inventory items partition into three urgent, two planned, and one monitor candidate.
Confirmed the earliest declared support horizon is five months and the urgent list is deterministically sorted.
Recomputed Exercise 2 sequential resolution range as 25 to 41 months.
Recomputed Exercise 2 decision-slack range against 30 months as negative 11 to positive 5 months.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Synthetic thresholds and point months omit consequence, uncertainty, service obligations, total feasibility, demand, stock, actual use, and authority.

evidence: Confirmed product discontinuance does not entail immediate unavailability, while current sale does not entail adequate future support.
Confirmed positive point-estimate slack does not entail low risk when horizons and lead times are uncertain.
Confirmed catalog or dimensional equality does not entail material/process/firmware/reliability/security/evidence equivalence.
Confirmed a lifetime purchase does not entail preserved tools, knowledge, rights, compatibility, authenticity, or usable lifetime.
Confirmed qualification and new-production incorporation do not entail resolution across field, spare, repair, recovery, supplier, or customer effectivity.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter consistently limits inferences from notices, inventories, roadmaps, stock counts, vendor support, qualification, and preservation.

evidence: Challenged nominal versus extended service, uncertain demand, attrition/repair yield, shelf/storage degradation, counterfeit and broker pressure, lot/site/subtier changes, stock loss, and surplus disposition.

Challenged software dependencies, compilers/build/signing, operating systems/databases/cloud APIs, certificates, data formats/models, test/calibration equipment, facilities, licenses/rights, and concentrated skill loss.

Challenged unsupported-but-contained operation, imperfect isolation, vendor roadmap changes, qualification failure, mixed versions, offline fleets, spares, repairs, recovery environments, and regulated/customer effectivity.

Challenged virtualization without rights/peripherals/data/security, archives without interpreters, newest-technology bias, duplicated redesign, false avoided-cost precision, and retirement without downstream disposition.
Reviewed all ten examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, uncertainty, evidence limits, effectivity, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real resolution needs applicable system/domain, product-support, parts/materials, supplier/manufacturing, software/data/platform, security/safety, reliability, V&V, logistics, contracts/rights, records, finance, operations, and technical-authority expertise.

evidence: Confirmed capability/service/records horizons and exact configurations/populations precede obsolescence classification.
Confirmed inventory covers end items and enabling hardware, software, data, services, tools, facilities, suppliers, rights, evidence, and skills.
Confirmed notices are verified against exact identity, contractual meaning, actual usage, dependencies, population, stock/demand, and source currency.
Confirmed alternatives include no action, support/isolation, source/buy/repair/reclamation, emulation, refresh/redesign, substitution, and retirement.
Confirmed every resolution integrates change impact, supply integrity, configuration, qualification/V&V, transition, effectivity, recovery, and old-state disposition.
Confirmed closure is observed across production, field, spares, repairs, software/services, recovery, customers, records, and continued monitoring.
invariant_checking.notes: No notice, BOM, vendor roadmap, stock quantity, broker sample, support contract, virtual image, redesign approval, qualification, purchase order, or new-production release is treated as sufficient alone.

proof_review.notes: No formal proof or theorem requires proof review; horizon arithmetic and inventory triage are bounded planning mechanisms.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is labeled or presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Executable output is labeled declared_support_months_only.
Fixture limitations disclaim service horizon, lead time, uncertainty, demand, stock, consequence, dependency, supplier truth, usage, security/safety, cost, feasibility, and authority.
Examples and exercises are synthetic teaching cases, not actual supplier forecasts, DMSMS dispositions, purchase approvals, equivalence findings, security authorizations, or certification decisions.
Official sources are attributed without claiming DoD, NASA, or NIST review, approval, or endorsement of this chapter.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic horizon sorting, source-backed guidance, internal review, supplier facts, qualification evidence, risk acceptance, and operational authorization remain distinct.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked relative obsolescence, service/support horizons, exact inventory and monitoring, uncertainty and decision slack, cross-domain exposure, resolution alternatives, lifecycle-cost and option reasoning, preservation, supply integrity, change control, effectivity, closure, and continued monitoring.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked DMSMS and parts/materials, software/services/data/tools/skills, authoritative sourcing, lifetime buys, counterfeit/storage, alternates, repair/reclamation, emulation, extended support/isolation, redesign/refresh, fleet transition, recovery, records, contracts/rights, metrics, and retirement.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from horizon and inventory through monitoring, forecasting, prioritization, option analysis, evidence, implementation, field closure, and retirement. Ten examples and five complete solutions cover physical, software, cloud, materials, calibration, data, counterfeit, skills, ML, and decision-sensitivity contexts.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external DoD/NASA/NIST expert, DMSMS or parts/materials specialist, supplier/manufacturer, product-support/logistics manager, software/data/platform owner, cybersecurity/safety authority, reliability/quality engineer, V&V/certification authority, contracts/IP/records specialist, operator/maintainer, financial authority, auditor, or other external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
